questions.question: Each core on a quad-core CPU has its own private mid-sized cache, while all four cores share one larger pool beneath it. Which level is the per-core private cache?
questions.explanation: L1 and L2 are typically per-core; L2 is the larger private tier below the shared L3.

questions.question: The last on-chip cache before a costly trip to main memory is shared by all cores and measures tens of megabytes. Which level is it?
questions.explanation: L3 is the large shared last-level cache sitting between per-core caches and RAM.

questions.question: A stick labeled DDR4-3200 delivers 3200 MT/s from a 1600 MHz memory clock because it transfers data on both edges of every cycle. Name the underlying RAM technology.
questions.explanation: DDR transfers on the rising and falling edges: 1600 MHz x 2 = 3200 MT/s.

questions.question: A video editor stripes blocks across two drives for doubled throughput, accepting that one drive's death destroys everything. Which RAID level trades all redundancy for speed?
questions.explanation: RAID 0 stripes data with no parity or mirroring — fast but zero fault tolerance.

questions.question: Two drives hold identical copies so either can fail with zero data loss, but usable capacity is only one drive's worth. Which RAID level is this?
questions.explanation: RAID 1 mirrors drives: full redundancy at half the raw capacity.

questions.question: A process touches a virtual address not resident in RAM; the OS loads its fixed 4 KB block from disk into a free frame and retries the access. Which memory-management scheme uses these fixed-size blocks?
questions.explanation: Paging maps virtual memory in fixed-size pages moved between RAM and disk on demand.

questions.question: On a mechanical drive, the delay before a read completes is dominated by rotating the platter and moving the actuator arm to the correct track. Which metric names this positioning delay?
questions.explanation: Seek time measures how long the head takes to position over the right track — a delay SSDs eliminate.

questions.question: An SSD stores 2 bits in each floating-gate cell — cheaper than one-bit SLC but with lower endurance. Which flash type is this?
questions.explanation: MLC stores two bits per cell; more bits per cell means cheaper, slower, less durable flash.

questions.question: A budget SSD squeezes 3 bits into every cell for density, trading write speed and endurance for capacity per dollar. Which flash type is it?
questions.explanation: TLC packs three bits per cell — denser and cheaper than MLC or SLC but less enduring.

questions.question: A full cache must evict an entry and discards the one untouched for the longest time, gambling that stale data won't be requested again soon. Which replacement policy is this?
questions.explanation: LRU evicts the least-recently-used entry, exploiting temporal locality.

questions.question: A 500 GB drive stores video files averaging 5 GB each; about how many files fit?
questions.explanation: 500 divided by 5 gives about 100 files, ignoring formatting overhead and hidden system data.

questions.question: An admin wants parity-protected storage that survives any single drive failure, with parity striped so usable capacity equals N minus 1 drives. What is the minimum drive count for this RAID 5 array?
questions.explanation: RAID 5 stripes data plus distributed parity and requires at least 3 drives.

questions.question: An industrial SSD must endure the most write cycles and the fastest writes, storing only one bit per cell at a huge cost per gigabyte. Which flash type is it?
questions.explanation: SLC's one bit per cell delivers the best endurance and speed at the highest cost.

questions.question: A deleted file's blocks must be flagged so the SSD can erase them in the background rather than stall on future writes. Which ATA command does the OS send?
questions.explanation: TRIM tells the SSD which blocks are unused so it can garbage-collect them proactively.

questions.question: A database server must detect and fix single-bit flips in RAM caused by cosmic rays — something ordinary desktop DIMMs cannot do. Which memory type does it need?
questions.explanation: ECC memory adds check bits that detect and correct single-bit errors.

questions.question: A RAID 5 array is built from five 4 TB drives. How much usable capacity does it provide?
questions.explanation: RAID 5 reserves one drive's worth of space for distributed parity: (5 - 1) x 4 TB = 16 TB usable.

questions.question: An SSD is rated for 600 TBW (terabytes written), and its owner writes 100 GB to the drive every day. Roughly how many years until the drive reaches its endurance rating?
questions.explanation: 600 TB = 600,000 GB; 600,000 / 100 GB per day = 6,000 days, or about 16.4 years.

questions.question: Task Manager shows RAM at 98% and heavy activity on drive C: because Windows is extending physical memory into a hidden system file at the drive's root. Name that file.
questions.explanation: pagefile.sys is Windows' paging file, overflowing RAM contents to disk under memory pressure.

questions.question: A phone has 20 GB free and records 4K video at about 350 MB per minute. Roughly how many minutes of video will fit?
questions.explanation: 20 GB is about 20,000 MB; 20,000 divided by 350 MB per minute gives roughly 57 minutes.

questions.question: Which cache write policy updates the cache and main memory on every write, trading speed for simpler consistency compared with write-back?
questions.explanation: Write-through pushes every write to memory immediately; write-back defers memory writes for speed at the cost of complexity.
